value.body: A data engineer builds and maintains the pipelines that collect, clean and move data into databases and warehouses, so analysts and data scientists can use it. Employers include IT services firms, product companies, banks, e-commerce and analytics firms. A typical day involves writing SQL and Python jobs, fixing failed pipelines, and modelling tables for reporting.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech (CSE, IT, Data Science), B.Sc Data Science or MCA

items.label: Common tools
items.value: SQL, Python, Spark, Airflow, cloud data warehouses

items.label: Typical work
items.value: ETL pipelines, data warehousing, data-quality checks

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often enter through IT services or analytics firms as trainee or associate data engineers, or move across from software or data analyst roles. Strong SQL, one programming language and a project on a cloud platform help.

value.title: At a glance
items: The work is closer to software engineering than to analysis; reliability matters more than models.
Next roles: senior data engineer, data architect, analytics engineering lead.
Tool stacks change often, so the specific tools in job posts vary.
